:::{#thm-surprisal-log-rarity}
#### Surprisal is the logarithm of the rarity

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv),
and let $x$ be a [value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-realization) of $X$ with $\P(X=x) > 0$.
Then the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of $x$ is the [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) of its [rarity](#def-rarity):

$$\surprisalf{x} = \logf{\rarityf{x}}.$$

:::

::: proof

$$
\begin{aligned}
\surprisalf{x}
&= -\logf{\P(X=x)} && \text{(definition of surprisal)} \\
&= \logf{\frac{1}{\P(X=x)}} && \text{(logarithm of a reciprocal)} \\
&= \logf{\rarityf{x}}. && \text{(definition of rarity)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
